Interpreting the June 16, 2021 FOMC statement through a New Keynesian/DSGE lens still points to an expectations-anchoring, highly accommodative stance: policy rates at 0–0.25% with average inflation targeting, ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases ($80B/$40B per month), and floor-system tools (IOER at 0.15%, ON RRP at 0.05%) to preserve easy financial conditions while “looking through” transitory inflation.

Incorporating the SLOOS nuances the transmission channel: banks report easing in residential real estate and HELOCs, and easing in several consumer categories (credit card, auto, broader consumer) with reduced minimum credit-score thresholds, and large banks easing for investment‑grade C&I—supportive for demand-sensitive sectors. However, standards remain tighter than pre‑pandemic for many consumer loans; foreign banks tightened standards for below‑investment‑grade firms (unchanged for IG); terms tightened for nonprime auto; and some large/small banks tightened C&I policies. CRE underwriting remains cautious across nonfarm nonresidential, construction, and multifamily segments. Netting these, credit supply is improving but uneven—particularly constrained for riskier borrowers—so the overall tone stays moderately positive but more balanced than a pure macro read.
